I have enough to write the full explanation.

## How it works

**Write side — keeping the index in step**

When a colleague edits an issue title, the request goes through `updateIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts:83-109`. That function checks tenant scope (`assertOrgScope`) and permission (`assertCan(actor, "issue:update", ...)`), persists the change via `issueRepo.updateIssue(input)`, and then — critically — calls `emit("issue.updated", {...})` from the in-process pub/sub bus in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`. The issue-service itself has no idea that search exists; it just publishes a fact.

`emit()` (`src/lib/event-bus.ts:54-72`) looks up every handler registered for `"issue.updated"` and runs them all via `Promise.allSettled`, so a failing search-index update can never fail the write itself or block other subscribers — errors are only reported to `onHandlerError` sinks.

The search side registers its interest in `registerSearchListeners()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts:137-183`. Its `"issue.updated"` handler doesn't trust the event payload's fields; it re-reads the row with `issueRepo.findIssueById(payload.orgId, payload.issueId)` and, if found, calls `indexIssue(orgId, issue)` (same file, lines 88-96). That guards against indexing a title from a write that partially failed. `indexIssue` calls `searchRepo.upsertSearchDocument(orgId, "issue", issue.id, [issue.title, issue.description ?? ""].join("\n"), issue.projectId)`.

`upsertSearchDocument` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts:18-59` looks up an existing row keyed by `(orgId, subjectKind, subjectId)` — not by the search row's own id — and either updates its `content`/`projectId`/`indexedAt` or inserts a new row. Keying by subject rather than row id is what makes repeated indexing idempotent. **What's stored in the index**: a denormalised `searchIndex` table (`src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`) with columns `id, orgId, subjectKind ('issue'|'comment'|'project'), subjectId, projectId, content, indexedAt` — `content` is just the title and description concatenated with a newline, no tokenization or ranking data. There's also a `"search.reindex_requested"` event handled the same way, for out-of-band reindexing.

`registerSearchListeners` is wired up centrally, not from issue-service — the actual subscription happens at module init, referenced by `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`, which is what keeps `IssueService` decoupled from `SearchService` per the doc comment in `event-bus.ts`.

**Read side — what a query goes through**

The colleague's search hits `searchAction` in `src/actions/search/search.ts`, a server action wrapped by `withAction` (checks auth/org via `getActor`, validates input against `searchQuerySchema`). It explicitly checks `can(actor, "org:read", ...)`, throwing `ForbiddenActionError` if not authorized, then loads the org via `getOrganizationSummary` and builds a feature-flag context with `buildFlagContext`. If the org doesn't have the `advanced_search` flag, it silently narrows `input.kinds` to `["issue"]` (comments dropped) rather than erroring — a deliberate "palette degrades" design per the file's comment — then calls `search()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts:46-86`.

`search()` does its own layered checks in order:
1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)` — tenant check.
2. `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", orgResource(input.orgId))` — permission check.
3. `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "search:query")` from `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` — a token-bucket keyed by `(orgId, bucketKey)`, capacity/refill scaled by the org's plan via `getPlanLimits`. **This is where a perfectly valid-looking query gets refused**: if the bucket has no tokens left, `verdict.allowed` is false and `search()` throws `Search rate limit reached; try again after ${verdict.resetAt}` — nothing wrong with the query itself, the org has just burst past its plan's search quota.
4. A second, query-content-based rejection: if `input.q` contains a `:` (field-scoped syntax like `status:done`) and the org's plan lacks the `advanced_search` feature flag (checked via `isEnabled`), `search()` throws `"Field-scoped search is not included in this plan"` — this one *is* about the query itself, deliberately refusing rather than silently treating the colon as literal text.

Only after passing all four gates does it call `searchRepo.searchDocuments(input)` (`src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts:83-121`), which does a plain `LIKE %q%` substring match against `searchIndex.content`, filtered by org, optional `kinds`/`projectId`, and paginated via keyset pagination (`toPage`/`keysetPredicate`). Results are mapped back into `SearchHit` objects (title = first line of `content`, snippet built by `snippetAround`) and returned up through the action to the UI.
